Title: Attention Is All You Need
Authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
Venue: NeurIPS 2017

Key Points

1. Main contribution
- The paper introduces the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms.
- It removes recurrence and convolution, which were dominant in prior neural machine translation systems.
- This design enables much greater parallelization during training and reduces training time while improving translation quality.

2. Core idea
- The Transformer relies on self-attention to model dependencies between all positions in a sequence.
- Instead of processing tokens sequentially like RNNs, it allows each token to attend to every other token in parallel.
- Since the model has no built-in notion of order, positional encodings are added to token embeddings.

3. Architecture
- The model follows an encoder-decoder structure.
- Encoder:
  - 6 identical layers.
  - Each layer contains:
    - Multi-head self-attention.
    - Position-wise feed-forward network.
  - Residual connections and layer normalization are applied around each sub-layer.
- Decoder:
  - 6 identical layers.
  - Each layer contains:
    - Masked multi-head self-attention.
    - Encoder-decoder attention.
    - Position-wise feed-forward network.
  - Masking prevents access to future tokens during generation.

4. Attention mechanism
- The paper proposes scaled dot-product attention:
  Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V
- Scaling by sqrt(d_k) stabilizes gradients when key/query dimensions are large.
- Multi-head attention projects queries, keys, and values into multiple learned subspaces and performs attention in parallel.
- This allows the model to capture different types of relationships simultaneously.

5. Positional encoding
- Because the model lacks recurrence/convolution, token order is injected using positional encodings.
- The paper uses sinusoidal positional encodings based on sine and cosine functions of different frequencies.
- Learned positional embeddings were also tested and gave similar results.

6. Why self-attention matters
- Self-attention offers shorter path lengths between tokens than RNNs or CNNs, helping model long-range dependencies.
- It requires fewer sequential operations, making training more parallelizable.
- For many practical sequence lengths, it is computationally efficient compared with recurrent models.

7. Training setup
- Evaluated on WMT 2014 English-German and English-French translation tasks.
- Base model:
  - d_model = 512
  - 8 attention heads
  - 6 layers
  - d_ff = 2048
- Big model:
  - d_model = 1024
  - 16 heads
  - d_ff = 4096
- Optimizer: Adam with a custom learning-rate schedule and 4000 warmup steps.
- Regularization included dropout and label smoothing.

8. Results
- English-to-German: Transformer (big) achieved 28.4 BLEU, exceeding prior best results by over 2 BLEU.
- English-to-French: Transformer (big) achieved 41.0 BLEU as a new single-model state of the art.
- The model required substantially less training cost than many previous systems.

9. Ablation and analysis findings
- Multi-head attention performs better than single-head attention.
- Larger models generally improve results.
- Dropout is important for preventing overfitting.
- Sinusoidal and learned positional embeddings perform similarly.

10. Significance
- This paper fundamentally changed NLP and deep learning by showing that attention alone can replace recurrence for sequence modeling.
- The Transformer became the foundation for many later models in language, vision, speech, and multimodal AI.
- Its emphasis on parallel computation made large-scale pretraining much more practical.

Concise Summary
The paper proposes the Transformer, a new neural architecture for sequence modeling built entirely on self-attention. By removing recurrence and convolution, the model trains faster, parallelizes better, and achieves state-of-the-art machine translation performance. Its main innovations include scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, and positional encodings. The Transformer’s strong empirical results and architectural simplicity made it one of the most influential papers in modern AI.
